newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber ends slightly lower in dull trade.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber ends slightly lower in dull trade.

text.p: CME lumber futures closed slightly lower in a quiet market after trading on both sides of previous levels early.

Traders said the market appeared to consolidate after recent sharp price swings and was awaiting the next move in cash lumber. Mills have kept asking prices high while wholesalers continue to discount wood to move product.
Futures held technical trend lines on the early setback, they added.
Futures closed $0.90 to $0.40 per tbf lower with March off $0.50 at $406.80 and May off most at $382.00 per tbf.

Futures will have normal trading hours on Friday. The CME Board of Directors earlier in the month approved a revised schedule that calls for agricultural contracts to trade normal hours instead of the earlier tentative schedule that called for an early close.
